full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Anwarul Haque, J.:  On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh this Rule nisi was issued calling the respondent Nos. 1-2 to show cause as to why the impugned Order No.10 dated 06.6.2006 passed by the Judge of the 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka in Artha Rin Case No.326 of 2005 and the prayer for rejection of application filed by the defendant under Section 21 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. In short, the case of the petitioner for the purpose of disposal of the Rule is as follows: 

 Plaintiff, respondent No.3, filed Artha Rin Suit for realization of outstanding loan to the tune of Tk.5,22,07,752.98 but this defendant petitioners, making their appearance, filed written statement in order to contest the suit and also prayed to resolve the dispute by "settlement conference" under Section 21 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 but the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat rejected such prayer and considering the written statement as admission of a case stated in the plaint. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat has passed the impugned judgment and decree amounting to Tk.5,22,07,752.98 under Section 13 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and also directed to pay the interest in terms of the provision laid down in Section 50 of the said Ain, 2003. 

 4. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners further submits that the recital of the written statement does not stand for admission of the claim of the plaintiff as required under Section 9(5) of the Artha Rin Adalaf Ain, 2003. Since in the instant case such an admission is lacking; the Court cannot invoke it's jurisdiction under Section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in order to dispose of the matter in the manner, prescribed by law. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision of a caw Md. Arfan Uddin Akand & Others Vs. Artha Rin Adalat and others reported in 15 BLT (HCD) page 343 where their Lordships have clearly observed that since there is, no admission made in written statement as contemplated in Section 9(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the same cannot be brought within the mischief of Section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The learned Advocate has - also referred another case of Mir Motiur Rahman Zihadi Vs. Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail and another reported in 15 BLT (AD) page 267. 

 10. However, considering the above facts and circumstances we are inclined to say that this case as has been made out does not come within the mischief of Section 130) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 and accordingly the decision taken by the Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat in order to dispose of the matter under Section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is absolutely illegal of course, the learned Judge of the trial Court is to dispose of the matter in accordance with law within 60(sixty) days from the date of receipt of the order without allowing any party to drag the matter in their own manner.
